I ordered some food that cost $15.50, and I gave the cashier $17 in total. That included a $5 note, a $10 note, and a $2 coin. I didn't have a $1 coin, so I used the $2 coin instead. If I gave $17 and the food was $15.50, the change should be $1.50, right? But the cashier gave me back 50 cents, which is less than what I should have received. So, they shortchanged me by $1. I was pretty sure I gave the $2 coin because I had prepared it and taken it out of my wallet. It's also a different size than a $1 coin, so I thought it was distinct enough that the cashier should have noticed it. But the cashier said they didn't see the coin anywhere. I was really sure I gave it to them, but they didn't acknowledge it. I ended up leaving because there was a line behind me, but I was upset enough to complain to my mother, who told me to forget about it because it's only a dollar. Now, I'm wondering if it's right or wrong for the cashier to forget the $2 coin. Is it their fault for not noticing it, or is it mine for not making sure they saw it? I think it's the cashier's responsibility to count the money they receive and give the correct change. If they didn't notice the $2 coin, that's their mistake. But on the other hand, maybe I should have been more assertive in making sure they saw the coin. I took it out of my wallet, but did I hand it to them clearly? Maybe I should have said something like, "Here's a $2 coin," to make sure they knew I gave it to them. Also, considering the amount is only a dollar, maybe it's not worth the hassle. It makes me question whether I should trust cashiers in the future or always double-check my change. I guess another angle is whether the cashier's mistake was intentional or accidental. If they didn't see the coin by accident, it's a simple mistake. But if they did see it and chose not to give the correct change, that would be wrong. I don't have any evidence to suggest it was intentional, so I should probably assume it was an accident. In terms of personal feelings, I feel like I was treated unfairly because I was sure I gave the correct amount, but the cashier didn't give me the right change. It's frustrating, especially when there's a line behind me, and I didn't want to cause a scene. But at the same time, I understand that sometimes mistakes happen, and it's not always worth the effort to argue over a small amount. I also wonder if there's a way to prevent this in the future.
